newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Unexploded bomb hurts 12 in Australian supermarket.
newsitem.headline: Unexploded bomb hurts 12 in Australian supermarket.

text.p: Twelve people were taken to hospital and 500 evacuated from a Sydney shopping centre on Friday after an unexploded chlorine bomb seeped out toxic fumes, firefighters said.
The bomb was discovered inside the Coles supermarket at Bondi Junction in Sydney's eastern suburbs at around 11.00 a.m. (2400GMT).
"It was giving off chlorine fumes, but it did not explode," fire brigade spokesman Paul Rafferty told Reuters. Police said earlier the device had exploded.
"The device was found inside the supermarket and has now been placed in a drum of water to stop it exploding, as it was giving off heat and chlorine fumes." Rafferty said.
Ambulance officials said 12 people had been taken to hospital suffering from the effects of chlorine inhalation, while 500 other shoppers and staff had been evacuated.
"Fire brigade officers will use the shopping centre's air-conditioning to remove the fumes and make the air safe," Rafferty said.
Both ambulance and fire brigade officials said a similar device had been found in another eastern suburbs shopping centre earlier in the week.
"But we don't know if they are related," said Rafferty.
